2.7.1 GENERAL INTRODUCTION

Gymnosperms (Greek: Gymnos-naked; sperma-seed) are naked seed plants because seeds are not enclosed in fruit. They are more ancient than the angiosperms in evolutionary terms. They were dominant in Jurassic and cretaceous period of Mesozoic era. Most of the gymnosperm have now become extinct.

The members are distributed throughout the temperate and tropical region of the world. They are widely distributed in the cold climates where snow, rather than rain, is the source of water. Gymnosperms are mostly perennial, xerophytic and evergreen plants. They are woody trees, shrubs and rarely climbers. Aquatic and herbaceous forms are totally absent. Theophrastus first used the word gymnosperm. 2.7.2 CHARACTERISTICS FEATURES OF GYMNOSPERM Some of the basic features of gymnosperm are given below:
1. Gymnosperms are evergreen woody trees or shrubs. 2. They are perennial and show xerophytic adaptation. 3. The plant body is sporophyte and differentiated into root, stem and leaves.
